### Matched-sample leverage specifications: Debt / Equity and Liabilities / Assets {.unnumbered}

To evaluate whether capital structure confounds the earnings-call disclosure signal, the baseline ANCOVA model (Model 0) is compared against specifications adding point-in-time XBRL leverage ratios (Model 1) on the exact matched subsamples (@tbl-call-beta-leverage-de and @tbl-call-beta-leverage-la).

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: false
from pathlib import Path
import pandas as pd


_lev = pd.read_csv(_p("call_beta_regressions.csv")).set_index(["model", "variable"])
_lev_samples = pd.read_csv(_p("call_beta_regression_samples.csv")).set_index("model")

def _lev_row(prefix, var, r2_row_label):
    m0 = _lev.loc[(f"{prefix}_M0", var)]
    m1 = _lev.loc[(f"{prefix}_M1", var)]
    return [r2_row_label, f"{m0['beta_std']:.4f}", f"{m1['beta_std']:.4f}"], [f"{r2_row_label}, p", f"{m0['p']:.3f}", f"{m1['p']:.3f}"]

def _lev_table(prefix, lev_var, lev_label):
    hist_row, hist_p = _lev_row(prefix, "hist_disclosure", "HistDisclosure, beta est.")
    surp_row, surp_p = _lev_row(prefix, "surprise_disclosure", "SurpriseDisclosure, beta est.")
    lev_m1 = _lev.loc[(f"{prefix}_M1", lev_var)]
    r2_m0 = _lev_samples.loc[f"{prefix}_M0", "r2"]
    r2_m1 = _lev_samples.loc[f"{prefix}_M1", "r2"]
    n_m0 = int(_lev_samples.loc[f"{prefix}_M0", "n_calls"])
    n_m1 = int(_lev_samples.loc[f"{prefix}_M1", "n_calls"])
    return [hist_row, hist_p, surp_row, surp_p,
            ["Leverage, beta est.", "—", f"{lev_m1['beta_std']:.4f}"],
            ["Leverage, p", "—", f"{lev_m1['p']:.3f}"],
            ["R²", f"{r2_m0:.4f}", f"{r2_m1:.4f}"],
            ["N", f"{n_m0:,}", f"{n_m1:,}"]]
```

```{python}
#| label: tbl-call-beta-leverage-de
#| tbl-cap: "Matched-sample leverage robustness: Long-Term Debt / Equity."
#| echo: false
from tabulate import tabulate
from IPython.display import Markdown

table_de = _lev_table("debt_to_equity", "debt_to_equity", "Debt / equity")
Markdown(tabulate(table_de, headers=["Variable", "M0", "M1"]))
```

```{python}
#| label: tbl-call-beta-leverage-la
#| tbl-cap: "Matched-sample leverage robustness: Total Liabilities / Total Assets."
#| echo: false
from tabulate import tabulate
from IPython.display import Markdown

table_la = _lev_table("liabilities_to_assets", "liabilities_to_assets", "Liabilities / assets")
Markdown(tabulate(table_la, headers=["Variable", "M0", "M1"]))
```

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: false
_de_hist_m1 = _lev.loc[("debt_to_equity_M1", "hist_disclosure")]
_de_surp_m1 = _lev.loc[("debt_to_equity_M1", "surprise_disclosure")]
_de_lev_m1 = _lev.loc[("debt_to_equity_M1", "debt_to_equity")]
_la_hist_m0 = _lev.loc[("liabilities_to_assets_M0", "hist_disclosure")]
_la_hist_m1 = _lev.loc[("liabilities_to_assets_M1", "hist_disclosure")]
_la_surp_m0 = _lev.loc[("liabilities_to_assets_M0", "surprise_disclosure")]
_la_surp_m1 = _lev.loc[("liabilities_to_assets_M1", "surprise_disclosure")]
_la_r2_m0 = _lev_samples.loc["liabilities_to_assets_M0", "r2"]
_la_r2_m1 = _lev_samples.loc["liabilities_to_assets_M1", "r2"]
```

Controlling for Debt / Equity leaves disclosure coefficients essentially unchanged ($\text{HistD} =$ `{python} f"{_de_hist_m1['beta_std']:.4f}"`, $\text{SurpriseD} =$ `{python} f"{_de_surp_m1['beta_std']:.4f}"`; leverage $p =$ `{python} f"{_de_lev_m1['p']:.3f}"`). Controlling for Liabilities / Assets results in minor shifts ($\text{HistD}$ moves from `{python} f"{_la_hist_m0['beta_std']:.4f}"` to `{python} f"{_la_hist_m1['beta_std']:.4f}"`; $\text{SurpriseD}$ from `{python} f"{_la_surp_m0['beta_std']:.4f}"` to `{python} f"{_la_surp_m1['beta_std']:.4f}"`) and changes $R^2$ by `{python} f"{abs(_la_r2_m1 - _la_r2_m0):.4f}"` (`{python} f"{_la_r2_m0:.4f}"` to `{python} f"{_la_r2_m1:.4f}"`) without displacing the disclosure terms.

## Appendix F: SEC Comment-Letter Inventory and Case Comparisons {.unnumbered}

This appendix documents the search for SEC staff comment letters that touch corporate AI disclosure, the classification of every letter found, and the case comparisons reported in the regulatory-scrutiny analysis.

### Search and classification {.unnumbered}

The EDGAR full-text index was searched for staff comment letters (form `UPLOAD`) and issuer responses (`CORRESP`) filed between 2022-01-01 and `{python} sec_cases["search_window"].split("..")[1]`. Search terms included "artificial intelligence", "AI", "machine learning", "generative", "large language", and hyphenated compounds ("AI-driven", "AI-powered", "AI-enabled"). Queries were restricted to the `{python} hd_n_universe` universe issuers, and every matching letter was read in full.

As shown in @tbl-g1-sec-letters, correspondence for eight universe issuers matched at least one term, plus Match Group (which joined after the panel date). Full-text review reveals that most matches do not concern AI disclosure. Two responses (Apple, Amazon) matched solely due to confidential-treatment page codes ("AI-001") or incidental references in climate-risk reviews, and are omitted.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-g1-sec-letters
#| tbl-cap: "SEC staff comment letters matching AI-related terms, S&P 500 (2021-01-01 universe), 2022–2026: what each letter actually asks, and whether it concerns the issuer's AI disclosure."
#| echo: false
from tabulate import tabulate
from IPython.display import Markdown
_rows = [[d["ticker"], d["company"], d["date"], d["filing"], d["subject"], d["relevance"]] for d in sec_cases["letters"]]
Markdown(tabulate(_rows, headers=["Ticker", "Company", "Letter date", "Filing reviewed", "Subject of the staff comment (from the letter)", "AI-disclosure relevance"]))
```

*Notes:* "direct" means the staff comment questions the issuer's own AI claims; "adjacent" means it requires AI-related revenue disaggregation without questioning AI claims; "incidental" means AI appears only as evidence cited inside a comment on another subject; "none" means the correspondence matched an AI term for an unrelated reason (a segment name, a climate-risk letter, third-party proxy materials). Accession numbers of the staff letters read: `{python} ", ".join(f"{d['ticker']} {d['accession']}" for d in sec_cases["letters"] if d["accession"])`.

### Matched-peer comparison for the direct and adjacent cases {.unnumbered}

For each case, annual reports are indexed in event time $k$, where $k = 0$ denotes the first Form 10-K filed post-letter and $k = -1$ the final pre-letter filing. Three control peers within the same two-digit SIC industry are selected via Mahalanobis nearest-neighbour matching on pre-letter log market capitalization, AI claim density, promotional density, and pre-letter claim trend ($\Delta k_{-2 \to -1}$). Control 10-Ks are aligned by filing year. With one direct and one adjacent case, @tbl-g2-sec-cases reports raw case comparisons without regression estimation.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-g2-sec-cases
#| tbl-cap: "Annual-report AI disclosure measures around the SEC letter: treated firm versus the mean of three matched industry peers."
#| echo: false
from tabulate import tabulate
from IPython.display import Markdown
_LAB = {"claim_density": "AI claim density (per 1k words)", "realized_density": "Realized-integration claims (per 1k words)",
        "quant_density": "Quantified-metric claims (per 1k words)", "specificity_index": "Specificity index (per frame)", "w": "Decoupling ($W$)"}
_KS = [-2, -1, 0, 1]
_rows = []
for t, c in sec_cases["cases"].items():
    pos = {k: i for i, k in enumerate(c["k"])}
    _rows.append([f"**{t}**", "Filing year of the 10-K"] + [str(c["year"][pos[k]]) if k in pos else "—" for k in _KS])
    for m, lab in _LAB.items():
        cells = []
        for k in _KS:
            if k not in pos:
                cells.append("—"); continue
            a, b = c["treated"][m][pos[k]], c["controls_mean"][m][pos[k]]
            cells.append(f"{'—' if a is None else f'{a:.3f}'} / {'—' if b is None else f'{b:.3f}'}")
        _rows.append([t, lab] + cells)
_hdr = ["Case", "Measure (treated / peers)"] + [f"k = {k:+d}" if k else "k = 0" for k in _KS]
Markdown(tabulate(_rows, headers=_hdr))
```

*Notes:* Welltower's letter (2025-04-28) reviews the FY2024 10-K filed in February 2025 ($k=-1$); the first post-letter annual report is the FY2025 10-K filed in February 2026 ($k=0$), so no $k=+1$ observation exists yet. Arista's letters (2024-07-25 and 2024-10-16) review the FY2023 10-K; $k=0$ is the FY2024 10-K filed in February 2025. Peers: `{python} ", ".join(f"{t}: {', '.join(c['controls'])}" for t, c in sec_cases["cases"].items())`.

## Appendix G: Sector, Cohort, and Rollup Disaggregation {.unnumbered}

The disclosure-posture, activity, decoupling, and credibility results above are computed on the pooled S&P 500 panel. This appendix disaggregates those constructs by two-digit SIC sector, filer cohort, and rollup method, using the same firm-year and activity-level tables read elsewhere in this thesis; no new constructs are introduced. Each table and figure below also writes the data behind it to `docs/analytics/`, and `docs/analytics/appendix_g_slide_manifest.txt` records which exported file backs which prospective slide.

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: false
import json
from pathlib import Path

def _gdir():
    d = Path("../docs/analytics")
    return d if d.exists() else Path("docs/analytics")

_manifest_rows = []

def _export(filename, obj, slide, viz):
    p = _gdir() / filename
    if filename.endswith(".csv"):
        obj.to_csv(p)
    else:
        p.write_text(json.dumps(obj, indent=2, default=float))
    _manifest_rows.append(f"{filename}\t{slide}\t{viz}")
```

### Does disclosure posture vary by sector, or mainly within it? {.unnumbered}

```{python}
#| label: tbl-h1-sic-posture
#| tbl-cap: "Mean disclosure posture and archetype composition by sector (2-digit SIC, top 10 by firm count), firm-year panel."
#| echo: false
from pathlib import Path
import pandas as pd
from tabulate import tabulate
from IPython.display import Markdown


SIC2_LABELS = {
    "73": "Business services", "38": "Instruments", "28": "Chemicals", "49": "Electric/gas/sanitary",
    "35": "Industrial/computer equip.", "67": "Holding/investment offices", "36": "Electronic equipment",
    "63": "Insurance carriers", "60": "Depository institutions", "20": "Food products",
    "37": "Transportation equipment", "62": "Security/commodity brokers", "13": "Oil and gas",
    "48": "Communications", "70": "Hotels",
}
m = pd.read_parquet(_p("firm_year_master_v2.parquet")).dropna(subset=["sic2"])
m["sic2"] = m["sic2"].astype(int).astype(str)
top_sic = m.groupby("sic2")["ticker"].nunique().sort_values(ascending=False).head(10).index
sub = m[m["sic2"].isin(top_sic)]

POSTURE_COLS = ["disclosure_intensity", "risk_orientation", "governance_orientation", "promotional_posture"]
posture_by_sic = sub.groupby("sic2")[POSTURE_COLS].mean().reindex(top_sic)
arch_mix = (pd.crosstab(sub["sic2"], sub["archetype"], normalize="index") * 100).reindex(top_sic)

```

Disclosure Intensity ($D$) is highest in business services and industrial/computer equipment and lowest in electric/gas/sanitary and holding/investment offices: sectors far from AI's core supply chain talk about it least. But every sector mixes archetypes: even electric/gas/sanitary, the lowest-$D$ sector, has Vocal Substantives among its firms, and business services has Defensive Disclosers alongside its majority of Vocal Substantives. Sector explains the general level of AI disclosure; it does not determine which posture a given firm within that sector adopts.

### What do different industries do with AI? {.unnumbered}

```{python}
#| label: tbl-h2-sic-role
#| tbl-cap: "Composition of disclosed AI activities by sector (2-digit SIC, top 10 by firm count), % of sector's activities in each role."
#| echo: false
from pathlib import Path
import pandas as pd
from tabulate import tabulate
from IPython.display import Markdown


m = pd.read_parquet(_p("firm_year_master_v2.parquet")).dropna(subset=["sic2"])
m["sic2"] = m["sic2"].astype(int).astype(str)
sic_by_ticker = m.groupby("ticker")["sic2"].agg(lambda s: s.mode().iloc[0])
top_sic = m.groupby("sic2")["ticker"].nunique().sort_values(ascending=False).head(10).index
n_firms_sic = m[m["sic2"].isin(top_sic)].groupby("sic2")["ticker"].nunique()

act = pd.read_parquet(_p("firm_activities.parquet"))
act["sic2"] = act["ticker"].map(sic_by_ticker)
act = act[act["sic2"].isin(top_sic)].copy()

def get_role(row):
    f = str(row["function_family"]); obj = str(row["object_family"]); tgt = str(row["target"])
    if f in ["product_feature", "content_and_media"] or "product" in obj or tgt == "customers":
        return "Sell"
    elif f in ["customer_service", "marketing_and_sales"]:
        return "Serve"
    elif f in ["software_development", "hr_and_talent"] or "copilot" in obj or "talent" in obj:
        return "Enable"
    elif f in ["it_and_cybersecurity", "fraud_and_risk", "governance"] or "security" in obj or "governance" in obj:
        return "Control"
    elif f in ["ai_compute_and_models", "research_and_product_development", "data_and_analytics"] or "compute" in obj or "analytics" in obj:
        return "Build"
    else:
        return "Operate"

act["role"] = act.apply(get_role, axis=1)
ROLES = ["Sell", "Operate", "Build", "Enable", "Control", "Serve"]
role_mix = (pd.crosstab(act["sic2"], act["role"], normalize="index") * 100).reindex(top_sic)[ROLES]

SIC2_LABELS = {
    "73": "Business services", "38": "Instruments", "28": "Chemicals", "49": "Electric/gas/sanitary",
    "35": "Industrial/computer equip.", "67": "Holding/investment offices", "36": "Electronic equipment",
    "63": "Insurance carriers", "60": "Depository institutions", "20": "Food products",
}
rows = [[SIC2_LABELS.get(s, s), int(n_firms_sic.get(s, 0))] + [f"{role_mix.loc[s, r]:.0f}%" for r in ROLES] for s in top_sic]
_export("appendix_g_sic_role_mix.csv", role_mix, "heatmap of sector x AI activity role", "heatmap")
Markdown(tabulate(rows, headers=["Sector", "Firms"] + ROLES))
```

Sell (customer-facing products) is the largest activity role in nearly every sector, but its share swings from a majority in industrial/computer equipment and instruments to a much smaller share in business services and depository institutions, where Operate and Control pick up the remainder. The AI-activity taxonomy is stable across industries; the mix that fills it is not.

### Do sectors differ in the amount of AI activity or in its grounding? {.unnumbered}

```{python}
#| label: fig-h3-sic-volume-grounding
#| fig-cap: "Median disclosed AI activities per firm versus mean AI activity grounding, by sector (2-digit SIC, top 10 by firm count). Point size scales with firm count; sector median lines shown for both axes."
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 7.0
#| fig-height: 5.0
from pathlib import Path
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt


m = pd.read_parquet(_p("firm_year_master_v2.parquet")).dropna(subset=["sic2"])
m["sic2"] = m["sic2"].astype(int).astype(str)
sic_by_ticker = m.groupby("ticker")["sic2"].agg(lambda s: s.mode().iloc[0])
top_sic = m.groupby("sic2")["ticker"].nunique().sort_values(ascending=False).head(10).index

wy = pd.read_parquet(_p("firm_year_washing_score.parquet"))
wy["sic2"] = wy["ticker"].map(sic_by_ticker)
wy = wy[wy["sic2"].isin(top_sic)]

SIC2_LABELS = {
    "73": "Business services", "38": "Instruments", "28": "Chemicals", "49": "Electric/gas/sanitary",
    "35": "Industrial/computer equip.", "67": "Holding/investment offices", "36": "Electronic equipment",
    "63": "Insurance carriers", "60": "Depository institutions", "20": "Food products",
}
g3 = wy.groupby("sic2").agg(n_firms=("ticker", "nunique"), med_activities=("n_activities", "median"),
                             mean_grounding=("grounding_index", "mean")).reindex(top_sic)
_export("appendix_g_sic_volume_grounding.csv", g3, "sector volume vs grounding scatter", "scatter")

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.0, 5.0), dpi=300)
ax.scatter(g3["med_activities"], g3["mean_grounding"], s=g3["n_firms"] * 4, alpha=0.7, color="#1D4ED8", edgecolor="white")
for s in top_sic:
    ax.annotate(SIC2_LABELS.get(s, s), (g3.loc[s, "med_activities"], g3.loc[s, "mean_grounding"]),
                fontsize=7.5, xytext=(5, 3), textcoords="offset points")
ax.axvline(g3["med_activities"].median(), color="#94A3B8", lw=1.0, ls=":")
ax.axhline(g3["mean_grounding"].median(), color="#94A3B8", lw=1.0, ls=":")
ax.set_xlabel("Median disclosed AI activities per firm", fontsize=9.0, fontweight="bold")
ax.set_ylabel("Mean AI activity grounding ($G$)", fontsize=9.0, fontweight="bold")
ax.set_title("Sector Disclosure Volume vs. Grounding", fontsize=10.0, fontweight="bold")
ax.spines[["top", "right"]].set_visible(False)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

Volume and grounding move independently across sectors rather than together: instruments and industrial/computer equipment combine below-median activity counts with above-median grounding, while business services pairs the highest activity volume with middling grounding. A sector that discloses a lot of AI activity is not thereby a sector that discloses it concretely.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-h4-sic-grounding-components

m = pd.read_parquet(_p("firm_year_master_v2.parquet")).dropna(subset=["sic2"])
m["sic2"] = m["sic2"].astype(int).astype(str)

act["Third-party attribution"] = act["source"] == "third_party"
COMPONENTS = ["Specific function", "Deployed / scaled", "Named product/process", "Quantified outcome", "Third-party attribution"]
comp_by_sic = (act.groupby("sic2")[COMPONENTS].mean() * 100).reindex(top_sic)

SIC2_LABELS = {
    "73": "Business services", "38": "Instruments", "28": "Chemicals", "49": "Electric/gas/sanitary",
    "35": "Industrial/computer equip.", "67": "Holding/investment offices", "36": "Electronic equipment",
    "63": "Insurance carriers", "60": "Depository institutions", "20": "Food products",
}
rows = [[SIC2_LABELS.get(s, s)] + [f"{comp_by_sic.loc[s, c]:.0f}%" for c in COMPONENTS] for s in top_sic]
_export("appendix_g_sic_grounding_components.csv", comp_by_sic, "heatmap of sector x grounding component", "heatmap")
Markdown(tabulate(rows, headers=["Sector"] + COMPONENTS))
```

The component that drops out first, in every sector, is quantified outcomes: even sectors above 85% on "specific function" and above 70% on "deployed or scaled" fall to single digits or low teens on "quantified outcome". Sectors do not withhold different evidence from each other; they withhold the same evidence: a number attached to the claim.

### Is the grounding decline within firms, or driven by new filers? {.unnumbered}

```{python}
#| label: tbl-h5-cohort-grounding
#| tbl-cap: "Mean AI activity grounding ($G$) by year: firms present since the first panel year (fixed cohort) versus firms in their first disclosing year (new filers)."
#| echo: false
from pathlib import Path
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from tabulate import tabulate
from IPython.display import Markdown


wy = pd.read_parquet(_p("firm_year_washing_score.parquet"))
first_year = wy.groupby("ticker")["year"].min()
y0 = int(wy["year"].min())
fixed_cohort = first_year[first_year == y0].index
wy["is_new_filer_year"] = wy["year"] == wy["ticker"].map(first_year)

fixed_traj = wy[wy["ticker"].isin(fixed_cohort)].groupby("year")["grounding_index"].mean()
new_filer_traj = wy[wy["is_new_filer_year"]].groupby("year")["grounding_index"].mean()
years = sorted(wy["year"].unique())
tbl = pd.DataFrame({"fixed_cohort_grounding": fixed_traj, "new_filer_year_grounding": new_filer_traj}).reindex(years)
_export("appendix_g_cohort_grounding.csv", tbl, "grounding decline: fixed cohort vs new filers", "line chart")
rows = [[y, f"{tbl.loc[y, 'fixed_cohort_grounding']:.3f}" if pd.notna(tbl.loc[y, "fixed_cohort_grounding"]) else "—",
         f"{tbl.loc[y, 'new_filer_year_grounding']:.3f}" if pd.notna(tbl.loc[y, "new_filer_year_grounding"]) else "—"]
        for y in years]
Markdown(tabulate(rows, headers=["Year", f"Fixed cohort ({y0} filers), $G$", "New filers' first year, $G$"]))
```

Grounding falls within the same fixed cohort of firms, not only because less-grounded firms enter the panel over time: firms disclosing AI activity since the first panel year show grounding declining across the sample period, and each year's new filers disclose at or below that year's incumbent level rather than above it. The AI-disclosure expansion documented earlier in this thesis is accompanied by declining grounding both because existing disclosers dilute their own claims over time and because new entrants join at an already-diluted level.

### Is the call-filing evidence gap sector-specific? {.unnumbered}

```{python}
#| label: fig-h6-sic-channel-gap
#| fig-cap: "Call-minus-filing gap in grounded evidence (mean of quantified outcome, named product/process, and named business function shares), by sector, firm x fiscal-year cells with >=3 activities in both channels (95% CI)."
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 7.5
#| fig-height: 4.2
from pathlib import Path
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt


m = pd.read_parquet(_p("firm_year_master_v2.parquet")).dropna(subset=["sic2"])
m["sic2"] = m["sic2"].astype(int).astype(str)
sic_by_ticker = m.groupby("ticker")["sic2"].agg(lambda s: s.mode().iloc[0])

GAP_FAMILIES = ["quantified_outcome", "named_product_or_process", "named_function"]
ch = pd.read_parquet(_p("channel_activity_cells.parquet"))
ch["sic2"] = ch["ticker"].map(sic_by_ticker)
ch = ch[ch["fy"].between(2021, 2026)]
wide = ch.pivot_table(index=["ticker", "fy", "sic2"], columns="channel", values=GAP_FAMILIES + ["n_activities"]).dropna()
wide = wide[(wide[("n_activities", "call")] >= 3) & (wide[("n_activities", "filing")] >= 3)]
gaps = pd.DataFrame(index=wide.index)
for f in GAP_FAMILIES:
    gaps[f] = wide[(f, "call")] / wide[("n_activities", "call")] - wide[(f, "filing")] / wide[("n_activities", "filing")]
gaps = gaps.reset_index()
gaps["mean_gap_pp"] = 100 * gaps[GAP_FAMILIES].mean(axis=1)

sic_counts = gaps.groupby("sic2")["ticker"].nunique().sort_values(ascending=False)
top_sic6 = sic_counts[sic_counts >= 10].index[:6]
SIC2_LABELS = {
    "73": "Business services", "38": "Instruments", "35": "Industrial/computer equip.",
    "60": "Depository institutions", "36": "Electronic equipment", "63": "Insurance carriers",
    "28": "Chemicals", "67": "Holding/investment offices",
}
rows = []
for s in top_sic6:
    v = gaps.loc[gaps["sic2"] == s, "mean_gap_pp"]
    se = v.std(ddof=1) / np.sqrt(len(v))
    rows.append({"sic2": s, "label": SIC2_LABELS.get(s, s), "n": len(v), "mean_gap_pp": v.mean(),
                 "lo": v.mean() - 1.96 * se, "hi": v.mean() + 1.96 * se})
fdf = pd.DataFrame(rows).sort_values("mean_gap_pp")
_export("appendix_g_sic_channel_gap.csv", fdf.set_index("sic2"), "forest plot of call-filing gap by sector", "forest plot")

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.5, 4.2), dpi=300)
y = np.arange(len(fdf))
ax.errorbar(fdf["mean_gap_pp"], y, xerr=[fdf["mean_gap_pp"] - fdf["lo"], fdf["hi"] - fdf["mean_gap_pp"]],
            fmt="o", color="#1D4ED8", ecolor="#93C5FD", elinewidth=2.0, capsize=4, ms=6.5)
ax.axvline(0, color="#0F172A", lw=1.0, ls="--")
ax.set_yticks(y)
ax.set_yticklabels([f"{r.label} (n={r.n})" for r in fdf.itertuples()], fontsize=8.5)
ax.set_xlabel("Call minus filing gap in grounded-evidence share (pp, 95% CI)", fontsize=9.0, fontweight="bold")
ax.set_title("Call-Filing Grounding Gap by Sector", fontsize=10.0, fontweight="bold")
ax.spines[["top", "right"]].set_visible(False)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

The call-filing grounding gap is positive in every sector with enough firm × fiscal-year cells to estimate it, and every confidence interval excludes zero: calls carry more verifiable detail than filings across sectors, not only in the pooled estimate reported earlier. The gap's size varies (largest in instruments, smallest in electronic equipment), but its direction does not.

### Do firms change disclosure posture over time? {.unnumbered}

```{python}
#| label: tbl-h7-archetype-transitions
#| tbl-cap: "Year-over-year archetype transition matrix, firm-year panel (row = archetype in year $t$, column = archetype in year $t+1$; % of row)."
#| echo: false
from pathlib import Path
import pandas as pd
from tabulate import tabulate
from IPython.display import Markdown


m = pd.read_parquet(_p("firm_year_master_v2.parquet"))
mm = m[["ticker", "year", "archetype"]].dropna(subset=["archetype"]).sort_values(["ticker", "year"]).copy()
mm["next_archetype"] = mm.groupby("ticker")["archetype"].shift(-1)
mm["next_year"] = mm.groupby("ticker")["year"].shift(-1)
trans = mm[(mm["next_year"] == mm["year"] + 1) & mm["next_archetype"].notna()]
ARCH = ["Vocal Substantives", "Governance-Led Disclosers", "Defensive Disclosers", "No AI"]
tmat = (pd.crosstab(trans["archetype"], trans["next_archetype"], normalize="index") * 100).reindex(index=ARCH, columns=ARCH)
n_pairs = len(trans)
stay_rate = pd.Series({a: tmat.loc[a, a] for a in ARCH}).mean()
_export("appendix_g_archetype_transitions.csv", tmat, "archetype transition matrix", "transition matrix")

rows = [[a] + [f"{tmat.loc[a, b]:.0f}%" for b in ARCH] for a in ARCH]
Markdown(tabulate(rows, headers=["From \\ To"] + ARCH))
```

Archetypes are sticky but not permanent: across `{python} n_pairs` consecutive firm-year pairs, `{python} f"{stay_rate:.0f}"`% stay in the same archetype on average, and Vocal Substantives and Defensive Disclosers are the stickiest, each retaining roughly three-quarters of their firms year over year. Governance-Led Disclosers is the least stable category, most often transitioning toward Defensive Disclosers rather than toward Vocal Substantives: governance-heavy language is more often a step down in disclosed activity than a step up.

### Do the results depend on the rollup method? {.unnumbered}

```{python}
#| label: tbl-h8-rollup-sensitivity
#| tbl-cap: "Share of disclosed AI activities meeting the named-product-or-metric grounding bar, by channel, under two rollup methods."
#| echo: false
from pathlib import Path
import pandas as pd
from tabulate import tabulate
from IPython.display import Markdown


act = pd.read_parquet(_p("firm_activities.parquet"))
act["grounded"] = act["evidence_type"].isin(["named", "metric"])

activity_weighted = act.groupby("channel")["grounded"].mean() * 100
firm_share = act.groupby(["ticker", "channel"])["grounded"].mean().reset_index()
firm_weighted = firm_share.groupby("channel")["grounded"].mean() * 100
tbl = pd.DataFrame({"Activity-weighted (pooled)": activity_weighted, "Firm-weighted (equal per firm)": firm_weighted})
_export("appendix_g_rollup_sensitivity.csv", tbl, "rollup sensitivity table", "table")

rows = [[ch] + [f"{tbl.loc[ch, c]:.1f}%" for c in tbl.columns] for ch in tbl.index]
Markdown(tabulate(rows, headers=["Channel"] + list(tbl.columns)))
```

Activity-weighted rollups (each disclosed activity counted once, so heavy disclosers dominate) and firm-weighted rollups (each firm-year counted once regardless of how many activities it discloses) answer different questions: "how grounded is the typical disclosed activity?" versus "how grounded is the typical firm's disclosure?" They give different levels here: the firm-weighted grounded share runs roughly 15–18 percentage points below the activity-weighted share in both channels, because firms with fewer disclosed activities tend to ground a smaller share of them.

Both rollups agree on the qualitative finding that motivates the credibility chapter: calls are more grounded than filings under either weighting.

### Do patents validate more than firm size and sector? {.unnumbered}

```{python}
#| label: tbl-h9-patents-controls
#| tbl-cap: "OLS of log(1 + AI patents, 2021-2023) on log disclosed AI activity, controlling for log market capitalization and 2-digit SIC fixed effects."
#| echo: false
from pathlib import Path
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import statsmodels.formula.api as smf
from tabulate import tabulate
from IPython.display import Markdown

def _pp(name):
    p = Path(f"../data/processed/{name}")
    return p if p.exists() else Path(f"data/processed/{name}")

m = pd.read_parquet(_p("firm_year_master_v2.parquet")).dropna(subset=["sic2"])
m["sic2"] = m["sic2"].astype(int).astype(str)
sic_by_ticker = m.groupby("ticker")["sic2"].agg(lambda s: s.mode().iloc[0])
size_by_ticker = m.groupby("ticker")["market_cap"].mean()

dim = pd.read_parquet(_p("firm_strategy_dimensions.parquet"))[["ticker", "archetype"]]
pt = pd.read_parquet(_pp("sp500_firm_year_ai_patents_oecd2025.parquet"))
pt = pt[pt["ticker"].isin(dim["ticker"]) & pt["year"].between(2021, 2023)]
pf = pt.groupby("ticker").agg(ai_pat=("ai_patents_oecd", "sum")).reset_index()

act = pd.read_parquet(_p("firm_activities.parquet"))
act["grounded"] = act["evidence_type"].isin(["named", "metric"])
af = act.groupby("ticker").agg(n_act=("text_hash", "size"), n_grounded=("grounded", "sum")).reset_index()

bench = dim.merge(af, on="ticker", how="left").fillna({"n_act": 0, "n_grounded": 0}).merge(pf, on="ticker", how="left")
bench["sic2"] = bench["ticker"].map(sic_by_ticker)
bench["market_cap"] = bench["ticker"].map(size_by_ticker)
bench = bench.dropna(subset=["ai_pat", "market_cap", "sic2"])
bench["log_ai_pat"] = np.log1p(bench["ai_pat"])
bench["log_mktcap"] = np.log1p(bench["market_cap"].clip(lower=0))
bench["log_n_act"] = np.log1p(bench["n_act"])
bench["log_n_grounded"] = np.log1p(bench["n_grounded"])
n_g9 = len(bench)
n_sic_g9 = bench["sic2"].nunique()

mod_act = smf.ols("log_ai_pat ~ log_n_act + log_mktcap + C(sic2)", data=bench).fit()
mod_grd = smf.ols("log_ai_pat ~ log_n_grounded + log_mktcap + C(sic2)", data=bench).fit()

tbl_rows = [
    ["Disclosed AI activities ($\\log A$)", f"{mod_act.params['log_n_act']:+.3f}", f"{mod_act.pvalues['log_n_act']:.1e}" if mod_act.pvalues['log_n_act'] < 0.001 else f"{mod_act.pvalues['log_n_act']:.3f}"],
    ["Grounded activities ($\\log G$)", f"{mod_grd.params['log_n_grounded']:+.3f}", f"{mod_grd.pvalues['log_n_grounded']:.1e}" if mod_grd.pvalues['log_n_grounded'] < 0.001 else f"{mod_grd.pvalues['log_n_grounded']:.3f}"],
]
_export("appendix_g_patents_controls.csv", pd.DataFrame(tbl_rows, columns=["regressor", "coef", "p"]),
        "patents vs activity, controlling for size/SIC", "table")
Markdown(tabulate(tbl_rows, headers=["Regressor (each in a separate model with log market cap + SIC FE)", "Coefficient", "p"]))
```

Disclosed AI activity predicts AI patenting even after controlling for firm size and sector: with `{python} n_g9` firms across `{python} n_sic_g9` SIC groups, a one-log-point increase in disclosed AI activities is associated with `{python} f"{mod_act.params['log_n_act']:.2f}"` additional log-patents (p < 0.001), and the same holds for grounded activities alone (`{python} f"{mod_grd.params['log_n_grounded']:.2f}"`, p < 0.001). The patent correlation reported earlier is not an artifact of large firms in patent-heavy sectors disclosing more of everything.

### Which firms embody or contradict the pattern? {.unnumbered}

```{python}
#| label: tbl-h10-vignettes
#| echo: false
from pathlib import Path
import pandas as pd

m = pd.read_parquet(_p("firm_year_master_v2.parquet")).dropna(subset=["sic2"])
m["sic2"] = m["sic2"].astype(int).astype(str)
sic_by_ticker = m.groupby("ticker")["sic2"].agg(lambda s: s.mode().iloc[0])
last_year = m["year"].max()
m_last = m[m["year"] == last_year][["ticker", "archetype", "disclosure_intensity", "sic2"]]

wy = pd.read_parquet(_p("firm_year_washing_score.parquet"))
wy_last = wy[wy["year"] == last_year]

sic_pick = "73"  # Business services: enough firms to span the full archetype range
prof = (wy_last[wy_last["ticker"].isin(sic_by_ticker[sic_by_ticker == sic_pick].index)]
        .merge(m_last[["ticker", "archetype", "disclosure_intensity"]], on="ticker", how="left")
        .dropna(subset=["archetype"]).sort_values("w"))
pick = pd.concat([prof.head(1), prof.tail(1)])

act = pd.read_parquet(_p("firm_activities.parquet"))
vignette_rows = []
lines = []
for _, r in pick.iterrows():
    lines.append(f"**{r['ticker']}** ({r['archetype']}, SIC {sic_pick}): $D$ = {r['disclosure_intensity']:.2f}, "
                 f"$G$ = {r['grounding_index']:.2f}, $W$ = {r['w']:+.2f}, {int(r['n_activities'])} disclosed AI activities.\n")
    q = act[(act["ticker"] == r["ticker"]) & (act["evidence_type"] == "metric")].head(1)
    if len(q):
        qr = q.iloc[0]
        txt = con.execute("SELECT paragraph_text FROM paragraphs WHERE accession_number = ? AND paragraph_index = ? LIMIT 1",
                          [qr["accession_number"], int(qr["paragraph_index"])]).fetchone()
        if txt:
            lines.append(f"> {txt[0][:280].strip()}...\n")
    vignette_rows.append({"ticker": r["ticker"], "archetype": r["archetype"], "d": r["disclosure_intensity"],
                           "g": r["grounding_index"], "w": r["w"], "n_activities": int(r["n_activities"])})

def _gdir():
    d = Path("../docs/analytics")
    return d if d.exists() else Path("docs/analytics")
pd.DataFrame(vignette_rows).to_csv(_gdir() / "appendix_g_vignette_pairs.csv", index=False)
_manifest_rows.append("appendix_g_vignette_pairs.csv\tcompany vignette cards (same SIC, contrasting posture)\tcomparison card")

from IPython.display import Markdown
Markdown("\n".join(lines))
```

Within the same sector, the same disclosure-intensity scale spans firms with almost nothing grounded behind it and firms with a quantified deployment behind nearly every claim. Same industry, same regulatory environment, same investor audience: the difference is what the firm actually reports having done.
